label: Manifold and Divergence
notes: This opening chapter spans printed pages 3 through 30 and introduces the central objects of information geometry. A family of probability distributions becomes a manifold, a divergence measures separation between points, and the dually flat structure ties these together into the framework the whole book develops.

label: Manifold of Distributions
notes: A parametric family of probability distributions is viewed as a smooth manifold whose points are distributions and whose coordinates are the parameters. Changing parameters moves smoothly along the manifold, so the tools of differential geometry apply directly to statistical models and their structure.

label: Divergence Functions
notes: A divergence assigns a nonnegative number to an ordered pair of points, vanishing only when they coincide, yet it need not be symmetric or satisfy the triangle inequality. The Kullback-Leibler divergence is the canonical example, measuring how one distribution differs from another.

label: Metric from Divergence
notes: Expanding a divergence to second order about a point yields a positive-definite quadratic form, which serves as a Riemannian metric on the manifold. For statistical models this construction recovers the Fisher information matrix, giving the manifold an intrinsic notion of distance and angle.

label: Dually Flat Structure
notes: A divergence also induces a pair of affine connections that are dual with respect to the metric. When both connections are flat the manifold is dually flat, admitting two affine coordinate systems linked by the Legendre transform of a convex potential function.

label: Generalized Pythagorean Theorem
notes: In a dually flat manifold a generalized Pythagorean relation holds: when a primal geodesic meets a dual geodesic orthogonally, the divergences add like squared lengths. This identity underlies projection theorems and the geometric view of estimation developed throughout the book.
